# windows_eventlog (Data Source)

Reads the observed state of an existing Windows event log (classic log or modern channel) on a remote Windows host without managing it.

The log is matched by exact name (`LogName`, matched literally — a `/` in a channel name such as `Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational` is part of the name). `record_count` and `file_size_bytes` are informational counters. `policy_override` reports whether Group Policy carries `MaxSize`, `Retention` or `AutoBackupLogFiles` for the log (`HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\EventLog\<log>`).

Returns an error when the log does not exist on the target host (for example a feature log whose role was uninstalled).

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Read the observed state of the Application log (read-only, no lifecycle).
data "windows_eventlog" "application" {
  name = "Application"
}

output "application_size_bytes" {
  value = data.windows_eventlog.application.maximum_size_bytes
}

output "application_retention" {
  value = data.windows_eventlog.application.retention
}

# Inspect a log managed by the windows_eventlog resource in the same
# configuration. The data source returns the observed live state, including
# the informational record_count / file_size_bytes counters and the
# Group Policy policy_override flag.
data "windows_eventlog" "managed" {
  name = windows_eventlog.application.name
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Exact event log name (`LogName`) on the target host, e.g. `Application` or `Microsoft-Windows-PowerShell/Operational`.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the log is enabled, as observed on the host.
- `file_size_bytes` (Number) Current size of the log file on disk in bytes, as observed on the host.
- `id` (String) Data source identifier: the exact event log name.
- `is_classic_log` (Boolean) Whether the log is a classic log, as observed on the host.
- `log_file_path` (String) Path of the event log file, as observed on the host.
- `log_type` (String) Log type as observed on the host (`Administrative`, `Operational`, `Analytic` or `Debug`).
- `maximum_size_bytes` (Number) Maximum size of the event log file in bytes, as observed on the host.
- `policy_override` (Boolean) Whether Group Policy carries `MaxSize`, `Retention` or `AutoBackupLogFiles` for this log, as observed on the host.
- `record_count` (Number) Number of records currently in the log, as observed on the host.
- `retention` (String) Retention policy as observed on the host: `overwrite` (`Circular`), `archive` (`AutoBackup`) or `retain` (`Retain`).

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
